verification.policy: A status of 'verified' means the behavior was checked, not that it looked right while somebody was reading the code. So an entry carries 'verified_on': for each platform, the suites whose tests cover it. An entry may be 'verified' only when every platform listed below appears in that map, because a command that only ever ran on one host is not a claim about the other one; and a suite that is not listed under a platform cannot be cited for it. The notes stay authoritative about what is missing either way - evidence for the parts that are covered does not certify the rest, which is why --require-full fails while any entry is not verified.

linux.how: make -C source/linux all check && make -C source/linux check-live

suites.unit: source/linux/tests/UnitTest.cpp - 728 checks of the parts that need no I/O: permission and mode parsing, masks, path handling, the transfer and synchronization planners, parameter and timestamp expansion, the stored-session file, the file-hash and HMAC helpers, and AWS Signature Version 4 signing (canonical request, derived signing key and Authorization header, pinned against botocore's vectors).
suites.script:
source/linux/tests/ScriptTest.py - the command line and script semantics against no server: abbreviations, switches, batch modes and exit codes, local listings, help, -log and -xmllog, and stored-session password encryption (a 'savesession -password' value
written as 'lscp1$' ciphertext under sessions.key and preserved across a
re-save without the key file).
suites.live-sftp:
source/linux/tests/LiveSftpTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestSftpServer.py - refused opens (wrong password, unexpected host key), operations the server denies, an interrupted download kept in '.filepart' and its resume (automatic and with -resume), the same for an interrupted upload, a continuation that must not splice an existing destination, a stale oversized staging file, resuming across a connection that died, option resume off disabling staging, and timestamps in both directions, and the shared stored-password format (a password encrypted by the GUI
module opening a stored session, a missing key file reported without losing
the value, and a core-written password decrypted by the GUI's reader).
suites.live-s3: source/linux/tests/LiveS3Test.py against source/linux/tests/TestS3Server.py - a throwaway S3 endpoint over TLS (the fixtures are committed) that re-derives every SigV4 signature with its own hmac/hashlib code: missing and wrong credentials refused (SignatureDoesNotMatch from the server, a secret-key complaint before any request), bucket and object listings through mkdir/put, rmdir refusing a non-empty directory while accepting a marker-less prefix and refusing the bucket itself, an upload/download roundtrip with a checksum, a resumed download that only completes if the server's 206 byte range was used, rename as copy-plus-delete with the source gone afterwards, remove of a missing key failing, stat reporting the server's size and time, and botocore signing one request the server must accept - the reference implementation tying both sides to AWS's own behavior. POSIX-only (curl against 127.0.0.1), so it cannot be cited for Windows.
suites.gui: source/gui/tests/ClientTest.js under node with jsdom - the real Commander page booted against a stubbed backend: rendering, selection, the editor, synchronization preview and run, search, the site manager, terminal, queue, host-key verification, synchronized browsing (the counterpart probe, following and refusing when the other side has no such folder) and drag and drop between the panes (payload, drop-target highlight, queued upload with the dragged names, same-pane drop ignored).
suites.live-dav: source/linux/tests/LiveDavTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestDavServer.py - a throwaway WebDAV endpoint over plain HTTP with Basic challenge authentication: a wrong password refused by the 401 retry before any command runs, listings built from PROPFIND Depth 1 properties (type, size, date - including on a server that refuses GET on collections), stat carrying the real size and modification time and a missing path saying so, mkdir refusing an existing name, rmdir refusing a non-empty directory and succeeding once emptied, rename through MOVE leaving exactly the destination behind, remove of a missing file failing, and an upload/download roundtrip with a checksum. The suite is standard-library-only and the client speaks plain HTTP, so it also runs where CTest does, Windows included; only Linux evidence is cited here.
suites.manual: Hand-run against the same server, kept here because no automated test does it yet: 'chmod -recursive' octal and symbolic over a tree, 'copyid' with an OpenSSH .pub and with a private key, 'put -append', 'get -append', -resumesupport=64 across a partial file, -speed=40, -preservetime=all on a directory, -xmllog= with -parameter. Reproduce with source/linux/build/linuxscp -batch -hostkey='*' -command="open sftp://testuser:testpass@127.0.0.1:12765/ ; ..." after starting the server.

suites.unit: linuxscp-unittest.exe, the same C++ checks, built and run by the MSVC and MinGW jobs.
suites.script: ScriptTest.py against linuxscp.exe - the command line, batch modes, exit codes, local listings and help, which is where a Windows path or separator difference shows.

windows.cannot_prove: No live transfer of any kind. The native PuTTY SFTP transport is not built for Windows, and the curl.exe that ships with Windows 10 and 11 has no SFTP or SCP support, so there is no way for the Windows job to open an SFTP session against the test server; a curl built with libssh2 would change that. What that leaves unproven: the transport itself, permissions and timestamps on uploads, a POSIX server's path semantics, and every extension whose answer only a server can give.

!.notes: Runs the command over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection and prints its output, like upstream 'call'. No interactive shell with a pty.

ascii.notes: Sets 'option transfer ascii' like upstream, with arity checks; the conversion is applied by get/put/synchronize and was verified byte-exact against a live server. No per-site transfer presets.

binary.notes: Sets 'option transfer binary' like upstream, with arity checks. No per-site transfer presets.

bye.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

call.notes: Rejoins and re-quotes the arguments and runs them over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection (the main SFTP session stays open). No interactive shell with a pty.

cd.notes: With no argument it goes to the home directory captured at connect time and prints the resulting directory, like upstream; 'cd <dir>' also prints. No directory history.

checksum.notes: Server-side check-file-name extension first, then a local sha-256/sha-1/md5/crc32 fallback through the PuTTY core; prints '<hash> <file>' like upstream. Verified live against a server without the extension (fallback path); the server-side path needs a server that implements check-file.

chmod.notes: Octal and symbolic modes ('u+x', 'a=r,go-w', 'u+s', 'X') and -recursive over a directory tree, symbolic links skipped; the mode is checked before the connection so a typo is reported even when offline. Upstream's script command passes an octal string only, so the symbolic forms and the recursion are an extension; verified against a live server that implements SETSTAT. Missing: owner and group changes, and upstream's per-site permission defaults.

close.notes: Single connection only; no indexed session close.

copyid.notes: Reads the session's private key (or the given key file: an OpenSSH public key, an OpenSSH private key or a PuTTY .ppk, foreign formats imported through the bundled PuTTY core) and appends its authorized_keys line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, creating the directory 0700 and the file 0600 and leaving an already installed key alone. Needs an sftp:// or scp:// session; an encrypted key asks for its passphrase in an interactive session and is refused in batch mode. The Windows build says it cannot read key files instead of doing nothing. Verified live for .pub, PEM private and duplicate input; the upstream command takes exactly one argument, ours also accepts none.

cp.notes: Server-side copy-data extension with a streamed fallback through the local host, recursive directory trees, multi-source into an existing directory and confirm-on-overwrite. Verified live via the fallback path; the native path needs a server with the copy-data extension.

dir.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format is the SFTP longname, not upstream's column formatting.

echo.notes: Plain token output. The line has already been through the upstream expansions - script parameters, %TIMESTAMP% and environment variables - because they are applied before dispatch; text in single quotes is left alone.

exit.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

get.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks, size/time criteria), -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, resume (binary only, rejected with ASCII), -resumesupport=on|off|<KB>, -append (native SFTP only), -speed=<KB/s>, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all]. Speed, append, resume and the time preservation were verified against a live SFTP server. Missing: transfer presets, -permissions on downloads and upstream's raw transfer settings. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

help.notes: Per-command 'help <command> / 'man <command>' with syntax lines and a general listing. Command names, including those in help, may be given as an unambiguous abbreviation.

keepuptodate.notes: Takes no direction word, like upstream, and accepts -delete, -filemask=, -transfer=, -interval=, -count= and -continue (keeps watching after a failed pass). Still a scripted poll loop, not the upstream background watcher: no file-system event source and no 'stop' command. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

lcd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

lls.notes: Local directories and simple wildcard masks; names-only output, not upstream formatting.

ln.notes: SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link), verified live. Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

lpwd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

ls.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format is the SFTP longname, not upstream's column formatting.

man.notes: Same as 'help': per-command syntax and a general listing, with unambiguous abbreviations accepted.

mget.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mkdir.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

mput.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mv.notes: Multi-source with an existing-directory target, rename in place and confirm-on-overwrite, like upstream.

open.notes:
URL sessions and stored-session names; an unknown host key is refused and reported on a HOSTKEY line so it can be pinned. No raw settings, SSH tunnels, session folders or session selection UI in the console client. A stored password that cannot be decrypted is reported and the
open continues without it.

option.notes: echo, batch (on/off/abort/continue), confirm, resume, transfer (binary/ascii/automatic), include/exclude (one mask, setting either clears the other, 'clear' resets), synchdelete, failonnomatch, reconnecttime (seconds or off, with automatic reconnect), editor, editmaxsize, and a listing when called with no name. Option and value names may be abbreviated when the abbreviation is unambiguous; masks, programs and numbers are never abbreviated. Missing: transfer presets and per-site persistence of script options.

put.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with WinSCP file masks, -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, -permissions=/-nopermissions, and the -resume, -append, -speed=, -resumesupport=, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all] switches of 'get' (append and resume are mutually exclusive and need the native SFTP transport). Verified against a live server. Missing: transfer presets and upstream's raw transfer settings. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

pwd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

recv.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

rename.notes: One source and one destination only.

rm.notes: Multiple files, masks and -onlyfile (directories are skipped with a status), no-match reporting gated by option failonnomatch, like upstream. No recursive delete, matching upstream.

rmdir.notes: Multiple directories in one command, continuing past failures; only empty directories, like upstream.

send.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

session.notes:
Lists the stored sessions from sessions.ini. The non-upstream helpers savesession and rmsession create and remove them, and 'open <name>' resolves a stored session, whose stored password (when one is stored) is encrypted under a sibling
sessions.key rather than kept in the clear. Missing: folder tree and raw
settings.

stat.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

symlink.notes: Alias of 'ln': SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link). Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

synchronize.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria=, -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (default from option synchdelete), -mirror (rejects 'both', resolves any difference toward the source), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count=; 'both' keeps a state record. Verified live. Missing: watch/background mode and upstream's conflict resolution UI. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

features.name: SFTP
features.notes: Native PuTTY transport on POSIX; Windows uses curl. SYMLINK, copy-data (with a streamed fallback) and check-file-name (with a local hash fallback) are implemented and were verified against a live in-process SFTP server; unknown extensions still fail explicitly rather than being ignored.

features.name: SCP
features.notes: Delegated to curl, whose SCP support depends on its build; no WinSCP shell-based directory and command engine.

features.name: FTP/FTPS
features.notes: curl transport and listing parser; no full upstream MLSD, TLS configuration, active/passive and server compatibility validation.

features.name: WebDAV
features.notes: PROPFIND-driven filesystem: Depth 0/1 listings parsed from the 207 multi-status whatever namespace prefix the server chose (resourcetype, getcontentlength, getlastmodified), stat through Depth 0 with real sizes, times and a missing path that reports as missing, MKCOL with named exists/parent-refusal messages, MOVE with an absolute-URI Destination and Overwrite semantics, DELETE with 409 read as 'not empty' - and rmdir checking the children first, because a DAV collection DELETE is recursive by specification. 'open' probes with PROPFIND and refuses a 401 after the --anyauth challenge round-trip (which also serves digest-only servers) and a 405 that means the server is not DAV at all; transfers stay on generic GET/PUT with curl's failure, range resume and timestamp flags. Missing: LOCK/UNLOCK, dead properties, COPY, If-header preconditions, and any Windows claim of its own (the suite is Windows-portable but no Windows evidence is cited yet).

features.name: Amazon S3
features.notes: AWS Signature Version 4 signing over curl (AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, pinned to botocore's vectors in the unit suite), s3:// session URLs with region from AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the hostname (s3.<region>.amazonaws.com or .com.cn) or us-east-1, and path-style bucket access: ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2 with delimiter and continuation, HEAD stat, get with range resume and Last-Modified preservation, put, directory markers with bucket-aware mkdir/rmdir, rename as copy-plus-delete, and explicit refusal of unsigned or wrongly signed requests. Evidence is Linux-only (the live suite's server and client path are POSIX). Not implemented: ACLs, versioning, multipart upload, storage classes, SSE options, object metadata beyond content, and a Windows functional claim.

features.name: Transfers
features.notes: Binary and ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks plus size/time criteria), include/exclude options, failonnomatch, resume with a -resumesupport= threshold (binary only), -append to add to an existing file, -speed= bandwidth limiting (pacing in the native engine, curl --limit-rate elsewhere), -preservetime with -preservetime=all for directories, and reconnecttime with automatic reconnect; ASCII conversion, speed, append, resume and times were verified byte-exact or by timing against a live server. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' temporary and are renamed into place only when complete ('option resume automatic|on|off', default automatic = upstream's rsSmart at 100 KB), which the live suite checks for both directions, for interruption and restart, for a stale oversized staging file and against splicing an existing destination. Missing: transfer presets and per-file progress reporting on the curl paths.

features.name: Synchronization
features.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria=time|size|either|none, -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (option synchdelete as the default), -mirror (any difference resolves toward the source; rejected with 'both'), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic applied to planned transfers, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count= and keepuptodate -continue; 'both' keeps a state record to tell changes from conflicts. Verified live. Missing: watch/background mode and upstream's conflict resolution UI; planned transfers stage through '.filepart' like get/put when the resume setting and the transfer mode allow it.

features.name: Sessions/configuration
features.notes:
sessions.ini site manager shared by the console and the graphical client: session, savesession, rmsession, 'open <name>', export/import and last-used tracking. Stored passwords are encrypted under a sibling 'sessions.key' (created
on first use, user-only access) in a format the graphical client reads and
writes too. Missing: folder tree, raw settings and the full upstream
configuration model.

features.name: Security/authentication
features.notes:
POSIX password/key/agent and host-key policy exist; an unknown or changed key is refused and reported instead of being accepted. GSSAPI is compiled out; proxy/tunnel configuration and curl fingerprint equivalence are incomplete. The graphical interface now verifies by default, pins on request and stores a pin rather than a wildcard, and its API is bound to loopback behind a per-run token with a Host check; there is still no user account; stored session passwords are encrypted at
rest under sessions.key rather than kept in the clear.

features.name: GUI
features.notes: Browser Commander with one persistent session per tab, dual panes, a transfer queue with progress/pause/cancel/retry, synchronization preview, remote search, a remote editor, the site manager and host-key pinning, driven by a loopback HTTP API behind a per-run token (Host-checked) over -server. Synchronized browsing (the toggle follows directory changes across both panes, refuses when the counterpart folder is missing, and keeps the pair aligned going up) and drag and drop between the panes (dragged entries carry a payload, the target pane highlights, dropping queues the upload/download with exactly those names, a same-pane drop does nothing) are implemented like WinSCP's Commander, both covered by the jsdom regression test. Still not upstream Commander/Explorer: custom commands, localization, and dragging from the operating system's file manager into the window.

features.name: Editing/search
features.notes: 'edit' downloads, runs the configured editor and uploads on change, with a size limit and a refusal when the remote file changed meanwhile; remote search matches name masks recursively. Missing: save/upload monitoring of local edits, full-text search, encoding handling and the custom command system.

features.name: Automation
features.notes: Console scripting with WinSCP switches, unambiguous command and option abbreviations, script parameters (%1%..%9% via -parameter), %TIMESTAMP% with relative offsets and formats, %NAME% environment expansion, and an XML action log (-xmllog=) recording every command, result, message and transfer with passwords masked. Missing: the WinSCP .NET assembly and PowerShell APIs, and equivalence with upstream's log format, which our log mirrors in structure but does not copy; the expansions are not applied to -server input, where the graphical client quotes literal paths.

features.name: Desktop integration
features.notes: Debian launcher/icons and terminal launch exist; no full upstream drag/drop, shell integration or extension system.

features.name: Localization/accessibility
features.notes: No equivalent upstream translation catalog and desktop accessibility verification.

features.name: Packaging/platforms
features.notes: Make/CMake and Debian/Windows builds exist; Windows curl may lack SSH protocols. Native builds do not establish functional parity.

linuxscp_additions.name: edit
linuxscp_additions.notes: Downloads the remote file, runs $LINUXSCP_EDITOR/$EDITOR or option editor, and uploads it back when it changed, refusing files over option editmaxsize and refusing to overwrite a file modified since the download. No local-side edit, no editor fallback chain or encoding handling beyond the installed editor. Upstream's script interpreter has no 'edit' command at the pinned commit, so this is a LinuxSCP command rather than parity work.

linuxscp_additions.name: savesession / rmsession
linuxscp_additions.notes:
Store and forget a named site in sessions.ini, which 'open <name>' and the graphical site manager then resolve. Upstream has no such script commands; it edits the configuration through its GUI and the .NET assembly. The password given with -password is encrypted under sessions.key
on save, and a stored value that cannot be decrypted is preserved across
an unrelated re-save.

linuxscp_additions.name: sessions
linuxscp_additions.notes: Plural alias of 'session' with no argument, listing the stored sites. Not an upstream command name.

linuxscp_additions.name: show
linuxscp_additions.notes: Recognised only to report that it is unsupported: the connection runs the SFTP subsystem, so there is no shell state to show. Not an upstream script command either.

linuxscp_additions.name: del, md, sync, quit, end
linuxscp_additions.notes: Extra aliases accepted for convenience (rm, mkdir, synchronize, exit, exit). Upstream registers 'dir' but not these, so they are not counted as upstream coverage.
